basics.name: Ernest Moyo
basics.label: Epidemiologist and Health Data Scientist | Bayesian malaria mapping and AI for health in Africa
basics.summary: Epidemiologist and health data scientist with 15 years in data and analytics, nine of them in public health with ministries of health across Southern and East Africa. Research Scientist with the Malaria Atlas Project (East Africa node, Ifakara Health Institute), PhD researcher in applied mathematics at NM-AIST, Co-Founder and CEO of 7Square Inc. (founded 2021) and Co-Founder of Hoop Africa Foundation. Trained as an actuary.

work.name: 7Square Inc.
work.summary: AI and digital-transformation company building software, AI agents and data systems for governments, NGOs and companies.
highlights: Clients in Tanzania, Zimbabwe, Namibia and the wider SADC region.

work.name: Hoop Africa Foundation
work.location: Namibia, Tanzania and the Democratic Republic of the Congo
work.summary: Foundation supporting neglected areas across Africa through research, innovation and development programmes.

work.name: Artificial Intelligence Technical Advisory Committees, Namibia
work.summary: Contributes to Namibia's National AI Strategy, leading on data governance, data quality, access and interoperability.

work.name: Climate x Fungal Disease programme, University of Oxford (NDM / Big Data Institute) and Wellcome Trust
work.summary: Systematic review on climate and fungal disease: inclusion criteria, search strategy and screening.

work.name: NGS Engineering Solutions
work.summary: Designed the NGS AI Readiness Audit and its online diagnostic.
highlights: 2026: facilitation team for an AI programme for young entrepreneurs at the Gordon Institute of Business Science (GIBS), South Africa.

work.name: Malaria Atlas Project, East Africa node (Ifakara Health Institute)
work.summary: Builds Bayesian and machine-learning models (Gaussian-process, geostatistical, spatio-temporal) that combine household surveys, DHIS2 routine data, entomological and satellite data into malaria risk maps.

work.name: Market Access Africa
work.summary: Country-level analysis of malaria treatment markets and stakeholder influence pathways across governments, national malaria programmes, regulators and financing bodies.

work.name: Ifakara Health Institute (host), NTD Modelling Consortium project with PAMCA and the University of Oxford
work.summary: Hosted by Ifakara Health Institute on a Neglected Tropical Diseases Modelling Consortium project with the Pan-African Mosquito Control Association (PAMCA) and the University of Oxford. Built predictive models for malaria and NTD elimination.
highlights: Designed and led the build of MosquitoDB, a vector-surveillance database, and its web decision-support tools.

work.name: Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI)
work.summary: Staff epidemiologist from July 2021 to March 2024, then consultant to December 2025.
highlights: Led malaria risk stratification and transmission-driver analyses in Angola, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Mozambique and South Africa, with the Malaria Atlas Project and Swiss TPH.
Designed national malaria data-use strategies for Namibia and Zimbabwe, and designed and piloted focus investigations in Namibia.
Led malaria programme reviews in Namibia and Zimbabwe; supported Global Fund funding requests for Zimbabwe, Namibia and Angola.

work.name: Delta Philanthropies and Higherlife Foundation
work.position: Head of Research, Monitoring and Evaluation
work.summary: Ran monitoring and evaluation across Zimbabwe, Lesotho, Kenya and Burundi for rural transformation, education, WASH, nutrition, public health and disaster-relief programmes.
highlights: Led the UNICEF Spotlight Initiative baseline on violence against women and girls in Zimbabwe (2019-2020).
Managed 8 to 12 staff across four countries.

work.name: Clinton Health Access Initiative (CHAI), with the Ministry of Health and Child Care, Zimbabwe
highlights: Led Zimbabwe's first national rollout of DHIS2 Tracker for malaria case and focus investigation.
Developed surveillance indicators and mapping guidelines; the focus-investigation guidelines were later adopted by other countries.
Trained health staff from provincial to ward level.

work.name: TTCS Global (SAP Gold Partner)
work.summary: Business-intelligence dashboards and analytics for clients in South Africa, Zimbabwe, Uganda, Zambia and Malawi.
